data.title: Golub Capital BDC outlines $0.29 per share NAV upside potential as it waives income incentive fee for the Dec. 31, 2026 quarter
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Golub Capital BDC (GBDC) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "The headline is that we're disappointed with GBDC's quarter." (CEO & Chairman David B. Golub) "Adjusted net income per share was $0.08. That's after the impact of $0.25 per share of net unrealized losses" and "almost all the loss related to fair value changes on 3 investments that we previously identified as problem credits." (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "For that reason, we've elected to waive the entirety of GBDC's income incentive fee for the quarter ended December 31, 2026." (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "Despite the disappointing quarter, we continue to be optimistic, in fact, very optimistic in our outlook for GBDC." (CEO & Chairman Golub) "We expect GBDC to benefit from the reversal in coming periods of a significant portion of its prior period fair value adjustments" and "there's approximately $0.29 per share in net asset value upside associated with debt investments in rating categories 4 and 5." (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "There were 3 drivers of NII this quarter." (COO & Director Timothy Topicz) "Adjusted net investment income per share was $0.33" and "investment income yield was 9.9% annualized in the quarter, consistent quarter-over-quarter." (COO & Director Topicz)
  • "NAV per share declined to $14 per share" and "we continue to position the balance sheet for flexibility to participate more fully in new originations going forward." (COO & Director Topicz) "We wrapped up the quarter with net debt to equity of 1.17x." (COO & Director Topicz)
  • "Based on our balance sheet at quarter end and assuming no changes in our investment and borrowing structure, every 50 basis point increase in base rates will result in over $0.01 per share of incremental earnings per quarter." (CFO & Treasurer Christopher Ericson)

Outlook

  • "My expectation is that higher-than-normal credit stress... it's going to continue as an industry-wide headwind for the next several quarters." (CEO & Chairman Golub) "The market trends have become more favorable. Base rates are going up, spreads have improved, documentation terms and leverage have become more lender-friendly." (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "Given the timing of contractual rate resets across our floating rate loan portfolio, we expect to see the impact of the September rate hike reflected in our earnings beginning in the 12/31 quarter." (COO & Director Topicz)
  • Compared with last quarter’s framing of "a continued period of elevated credit stress" and a gradual shift to "more lender friendly," management’s current-quarter language emphasized a specific near-term action (the Dec. 31, 2026 incentive fee waiver) alongside expectations for "reversal" of prior fair value adjustments. (CEO & Chairman Golub)

Financial Results

  • "Adjusted net investment income per share was $0.33" and "adjusted net income per share was $0.08." (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "Investments on nonaccrual status remained quite low at just 1.6% of the portfolio at fair value" and "a little more than 85% of our investment portfolio at fair value remains in our highest internal performance rating categories." (COO & Director Topicz)
  • "We did, however, recognize $0.25 per share of adjusted net unrealized and realized losses in the quarter" including "about $0.21" tied to markdowns on investments in portfolio companies "currently on nonaccrual status." (COO & Director Topicz)
  • "We ended the quarter with approximately $1.7 billion of liquidity" and "in the quarter, we successfully amended certain terms and extended the maturity of our syndicated corporate revolver to July 2031." (CFO & Treasurer Ericson)

Q&A

  • Kenneth Lee, RBC Capital Markets: "the investments on the risk grade 3 were higher than historical levels"—what challenges/commonalities? CEO & Chairman Golub: "we saw a series of repayments of 4s and 5s" while the company prioritized "repurchase of shares and a little bit of deleveraging," adding "Categories 1 and 2... have stayed very low."
  • Kenneth Lee, RBC Capital Markets: capital allocation priorities given better pipeline? CEO & Chairman Golub: "We're now in an environment where both are attractive" and "We're going to have to find the right balance."
  • Paul Johnson, KBW: are category 3s driven by new issues vs. existing? CEO & Chairman Golub: "we're not seeing migration" and "we're not seeing emergence of a bunch of new problems."
  • Paul Johnson, KBW: sensitivity to another 50 bps of hikes and software budgeting for AI? CEO & Chairman Golub: "in the range of 50 basis points... this is not going to move the needle in a meaningful way from a credit standpoint" and described software sales cycles as "some longer time frames to get sales done."
  • Robert Dodd, Raymond James: why do some restructurings keep deteriorating? CEO & Chairman Golub: "turnarounds are hard" and said the cycle will test managers "when you get too many of these in your portfolio."
  • Robert Dodd, Raymond James: confidence in a sustained activity rebound? CEO & Chairman Golub: "let's all be humble" but cited drivers including "the average PortCo... is about 7 years old" and "the economy is strong."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was neutral-to-skeptical, repeatedly pressing on credit migration, category 3 watch items, and durability of origination recovery, including whether troubled assets "just continues to have more and more problems" (Robert Dodd, Raymond James).
  • Management tone was slightly negative on the quarter but forward-leaning on future earnings setup, combining "we're disappointed" with "very optimistic" and anchoring responses around identified problem credits and improved new-deal economics. (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s "better than it looks" framing, management’s current-quarter posture was more candid about results and more specific about corrective steps (fee waiver) and a quantified reversal expectation ("$0.29 per share"). (CEO & Chairman Golub)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Profitability narrative shifted from Q3’s "much better than last quarter" with "Adjusted net income per share was $0.22" (CEO & Chairman Golub, prior call) to Q4’s "disappointed" outcome driven by unrealized marks on "3 investments" already flagged as problems. (CEO & Chairman Golub, current call)
  • Portfolio indicators showed modest movement: nonaccruals were "1.9%" last quarter (COO & Director Topicz, prior call) and "1.6%" this quarter (COO & Director Topicz, current call), while management attributed the category-3 mix change largely to repayments and limited new investing.
  • Capital allocation stayed centered on deleveraging and buybacks, but Q4 Q&A emphasized the growing tension of choosing between discounted repurchases and improving origination opportunities. (CEO & Chairman Golub)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Credit stress is currently running higher than normal" and "about twice normal levels," with management linking the quarter’s volatility to downside mark movement in problem credits. (CEO & Chairman Golub)
  • "Sponsors and borrowers continue to experience a high level of macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty" contributing to "lower sponsor-backed M&A activity." (Senior Managing Director Robert Tuchscherer)
  • "Junior debt is going to likely be a meaningful driver of underperformance in the coming period" while noting GBDC has "relatively little" exposure. (CEO & Chairman Golub)

Final Takeaway

Management characterized the quarter as a fair-value-driven setback concentrated in three previously identified problem credits, while highlighting stable net investment income, reduced nonaccrual percentage, balance sheet flexibility through deleveraging, and a near-term incentive fee waiver for the December 31, 2026 quarter. Leadership also pointed to improving deal terms and a quantified potential reversal of prior fair value adjustments, while cautioning that elevated credit stress could remain a headwind for several quarters.

data.title: Global GDP to grow 2.8% in 2027, with corporate earnings growth slowing and stocks rallying – Goldman Sachs
data.description:
Goldman Sachs Research forecasted global GDP will grow 2.8% in 2027, up from 2.7% this year, as declining energy prices and robust artificial intelligence investment outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

The economies of the US, Japan, and the UK are among those projected to grow faster than the consensus of economist estimates, according to the investment bank's research division.

The risks to that forecast "are tilted to the downside," said Jan Hatzius, chief economist and head of Goldman Sachs Research.

Renewed Middle East escalation could spark another energy price surge, large fiscal deficits could push up long-term yields, especially in France, and AI capital expenditures could fall short of expectations due to capacity constraints, regulation, credit market stress, or weaker demand, he said.

Japan stands out as an exception, where consumption tax cuts, defense spending, and investment plans are forecast to boost GDP growth by 0.7 percentage point, according to the economist.

AI investment is expected to keep boosting growth, with Goldman analysts forecasting that nominal global AI investment will rise to $1.8T in 2027 from $1.1T this year, mostly driven by an over $500B increase in U.S. hardware spending.

The economists estimated that AI investment will boost GDP growth by 0.4 percentage point globally. Under the firm's baseline forecast for a steady decline in energy prices, inflation should slow in 2027, with Hatzius expecting core PCE inflation to ease from 3.2% at the end of 2026 to 2.4% at the end of 2027.

Stock markets from New York to Tokyo are expected to extend their rally in 2027, even as corporate earnings growth and AI investment slow in most regions, said Peter Oppenheimer, chief global equity strategist in Goldman Sachs Research.

"We expect the equity bull market to continue," Oppenheimer said, though he also anticipated more volatility than in recent years.

In the U.S., corporate earnings growth is expected to slow from 36% to 11%, in part because hyperscaler capital spending is expected to grow more slowly and energy prices are easing, according to the strategist.

The Goldman team highlighted three key investment themes for 2027. Growth stocks (VUG), (IWF), (IVW) present opportunities as the price-to-earnings ratio for technology stocks (XLK), (VGT) globally has fallen sharply, now sitting in the 20th percentile of its historical band over the past 20 years, the analysts noted.

Defensive equities could also offer opportunities, with Oppenheimer suggesting a focus on companies that benefit from lower bond yields, such as U.S. firms that consistently buy back their stock, while Europe (VGK), (IEV) stands to gain the most from cheaper energy prices.

data.title: KFC franchisee declares bankruptcy
data.description:
A major franchisee of Yum Brands’ (YUM) KFC restaurants has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, citing declining sales and rising costs.

Tasty Chick’n LLC and its affiliates filed Monday in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas in an effort to prevent the parent company of KFC from terminating its franchise agreement and seizing its KFC and co-branded Taco Bell restaurants. The franchisee currently owes close to $16M in unpaid royalties to Yum (YUM) owed since November 2025. The company also owes $67.2M to lenders.

Yum (YUM) notified the franchisee nearly a year ago that it was in default of its franchise agreements.

According to court papers, Tasty Chick’n has closed or will close 72 KFC restaurants co-branded Taco Bells and has requested the court to let it drop all its leases.  

Tasty Chick’n is the most recent of major franchisees going bankrupt over the past several months. Bloomin’ Brands’ (BLMN) largest Outback Restaurant franchisee, Out West, filed for bankruptcy protection in November, while Wendy’s (WEN) has surfaced as the stalking horse bidder for Meritage Hospitality Group’s restaurants.

data.title: Starboard Value's top holding assigned Buy rating by Seeking Alpha's quant rating
data.description:
New York-based Starboard Value reported a third-quarter portfolio value of $4.67B, up 3% sequentially. Compared to the year-ago period, the portfolio value decreased 12% despite an increase in its holdings to 22 from 20.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, Starboard’s top holdings remained unchanged, with iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF (IJH), Qorvo, and Kenvue continuing to occupy the top three spots. 

The fund, however, cranked up its holdings in iShares to 12.20M shares from 8.88M in the previous quarter—accounting for 19% of its total holdings. Starboard also increased Riot Platforms (RIOT) holdings to 10.50M shares from 10.11M.

Meanwhile, the fund slashed its holdings in Dynatrace (DT), Match Group (MTCH), and News Corp (NWS), among others.

data.title: Google expands Project Genie with real-time editing of AI-generated worlds
data.description:
Google (GOOGL) is expanding access to Project Genie, an experimental AI tool that lets users create and explore interactive virtual worlds, adding real-time editing, audio, and longer exploration sessions.

The updated experience will be available to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, the company said Thursday.

The company said the technology remains experimental. "We are actively tackling key challenges such as camera latency, intricate physical interactions, real-time audio precision, and long-term scene permanence," Google said in its blogpost.

The update introduces access to Genie 4, Google's latest world model, which allows users to modify environments through text prompts while exploring them. Users can change weather conditions, add characters, or alter events as they move through a generated world. The model also generates audio, including background sounds and character dialogue, that changes with the scene.

Google is also extending the capabilities of Genie 3, allowing users to explore generated worlds for up to three minutes per session, compared with 60 seconds previously. Users can also link multiple worlds together and create environments using 360-degree panoramic images.

Google said generated video and audio include SynthID watermarks and that inputs and outputs are screened for safety.

data.title: Europe’s clean-energy push deepens dependence on Chinese technology
data.description:
Europe’s transition away from imported fossil fuels is creating a different overseas dependence: Chinese clean-energy equipment. Wind and solar generated more EU electricity than fossil fuels last year, but inexpensive Chinese technology is helping drive that expansion while squeezing European manufacturers, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

For investors, Europe’s response could reshape competition across solar, batteries and wind power. Procurement preferences and subsidies may support domestic suppliers, while restrictions on cheaper imports could raise developers’ costs and slow installations. Policy decisions will help determine which businesses capture the transition’s growth.

China produces at least 80% of the world’s solar products and lithium-ion batteries. European wind-turbine manufacturers retain a stronger position, although they rely heavily on Chinese rare-earth magnets.

The EU has proposed favoring European-made solar panels, turbines and batteries in public contracts. Some governments also subsidize purchases of locally manufactured equipment, but substantial price differences make it difficult to change buying habits.

Chinese wind equipment costs 30% to 45% less to manufacture, while Chinese electrolyzers used to produce hydrogen can cost less than half their European equivalents. Protecting domestic production could therefore make Europe’s climate goals more expensive to achieve.

Security concerns are adding pressure for restrictions. The EU has barred Chinese inverters from EU-funded projects and is considering broader limits. These devices connect solar generation to usable electricity, and experts warn coordinated cyberattacks could disrupt power supplies.

Europe’s challenge is deciding which industries warrant support. Bruegel researcher Simone Tagliapietra argues that inexpensive solar imports have accelerated deployment and created installation jobs, while Europe could concentrate industrial investment in stronger businesses such as cables and wind turbines.

data.title: Skydance is combining the Warner Bros. and Paramount TV studios
data.description:
Skydance Corporation (SKYD) is already making major post-merger moves. The media giant announced that it will combine Warner Bros. Television and Paramount Television Studios into a single TV studio entity that will have more than 100 productions under its control. The new organization will be called Warner Bros. Television Studios and will launch early next year. 

The merged studio unit is being co-led by Channing Dungey (head of Warner Bros. Television Group) and Matt Thunell (president of Paramount Television Studios). Both will report to George Cheeks, who oversees Skydance's (SKYD) broader television operations.

As part of the same broader TV restructuring, Skydance (SKYD) has also folded its television animation assets (Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios, Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe, and Nickelodeon Animation Studios) into a single division called Skydance Television Animation.

The consolidation is a major piece of Skydance's (SKYD) post-merger integration strategy aimed at achieving $6B in annual synergies within three years. Separately, Skydance (SKYD) is considering combining Paramount+ and HBO Max into one streaming service.

Shares of Skydance (SKYD) are up about 2% since the mega-merger closed.

data.title: U.S. indexes are mixed after Nvidia earnings; gold declines
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages were mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia (NVDA) reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. Investor sentiment was shaken as they now turn to upcoming FOMC minutes from the last meeting.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was +0.8, and the blue-chip Dow (DJI) was -0.7%.

Nvidia shares seesawed and were last -2.1% after the company reported Q3 results that showed a 75% year-over-year revenue growth estimate for the fiscal year ending January 2028.

“Nvidia earnings are a tech bellwether in the same way that GDP tells you what the economy was doing three months ago,” said Dario Perkins, managing director of Global Macro at TS Lombard.

“Technology is down to 35.4% of the S&P 500 and more than 19% off the recent highs. Still outperforming the S&P 500 YTD though,” Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, added.

On the economic side, U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% month-over-month in October, more than expected, while permits increased less than consensus anticipated. In addition, the October U.S. Pending Home Sales Index slid -4.7% this month, more than expected.

Later today, the Federal Reserve will release the minutes from its last meeting. Bank of America expects the minutes to reveal a deeper divide over the decision to be on rate hold than the 10-2 vote suggested.

The gold spot price (XAUUSD:CUR) is down 2.9% on Wednesday due to hawkish monetary policy expectations and the ongoing stock market weakness.

Over to the bond market, yields were lower. The 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) declined 6 basis points to 5.06%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) also was 3 basis points lower at 4.79%. The 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) was 5 basis points lower at 5.41%.

Oil prices were mostly lower. Crude oil futures (CL1:COM) were $82, while Brent (CO1:COM) was $91 per barrel.

data.title: Lyft adds 9% following CEO's appearance at RBC conference
data.description:
Shares of Lyft Inc. rose about 8% on Wednesday, a day after Chief Executive David Risher told investors at RBC Capital Markets’ Global Technology, Internet, Media and Telecommunications Conference that the ride-hailing company had made a “strong start to the quarter.” The stock rose $1.49 to reach $18.21 in afternoon trading.

Speaking Tuesday, Risher said the fourth quarter was going “possibly even slightly stronger than we expected,” though he told analysts not to change their models. He credited the momentum to rider incentives Lyft spent on in the third quarter, saying their effects were lasting weeks and months and were stronger than the company had expected. He also repeated that growth in Lyft’s North American rideshare business, which has accelerated for two straight quarters, “will accelerate again next quarter.”

data.title: Fervo Energy rises after signing 105 MW Utah transmission agreement
data.description:
Fervo Energy (FRVO) rose 3.8% in Wednesday's trading after saying it executed a new 105 MW transmission service agreement with Longroad Energy for development of the Cape Station geothermal project in Beaver County, Utah, where Fervo has been developing geothermal energy infrastructure.

Fervo (FRVO) said the deal gives it long-term, firm delivery rights on the Milford Gen Lead line and builds on the parties' existing 400 MW arrangement, raising Cape Station's total contracted long-term firm transmission capacity to 505 MW.

"Longroad has worked alongside Fervo since its first efforts in Beaver County, and we're excited to collaborate again," Longroad Energy's chief development officer said. "Providing transmission service for this next phase helps deliver clean, around-the-clock power to the grid."

The transmission service agreement is expected to begin in 2028, subject to regulatory approvals.
